three_question_gate.executes: tests/conftest.py imports tests/netguard.py and calls install() at conftest import time (a conftest IS a pytest plugin). Enforcement of the swallowing class is an autouse fixture, _netguard_strict, in the same conftest.
three_question_gate.triggers: every pytest run of apps/cockpit/backend, unconditionally. testpaths=tests means tests/conftest.py is always imported. Default mode is strict; it is NOT opt-in and needs no flag.
three_question_gate.fails: a test reaching a non-loopback host gets socket.gaierror (NetworkBlocked). If it needs the call it fails; if it swallows the error the autouse fixture errors it at teardown. Either way pytest exits non-zero and the 'Python tests (cockpit backend)' job fails. Running in production CI today: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `python -m pytest -q` from apps/cockpit/backend with no COCKPIT_NETGUARD override, so the strict default applies. Verified on CI run 32395620227 that the guard armed on ubuntu-latest and reported its count.
three_question_gate.bypasses: 1) a child process (measured, leaks); 2) COCKPIT_NETGUARD=off, an explicit recorded env choice; 3) @pytest.mark.allow_network, used only by the guard's own probes; 4) the 22 nodeids frozen in tests/netguard_baseline.txt; 5) a socket opened before conftest line 41; 6) any harness that does not load tests/conftest.py; 7) a test that itself patches and restores socket.getaddrinfo.

notes.count_method: Enumerated under block mode, not report mode. Report mode found only 17 because successful calls populate an in-process cache and the remaining 38 tests never touch the socket (test_zone_atoms alone collapses 21 -> 1). Blocking is the sound enumerator; a passive sweep under-counts this suite threefold.
notes.cross_validation: The 51 were derived independently on two platforms, GitHub ubuntu-latest/py3.12 (CI run 32395620227) and Windows 3.12.10, and the nodeid sets were IDENTICAL.
notes.bucket_legitimate_local_caveat: 1934 is tests that touched LOOPBACK, dominated by asyncio's self-pipe via socket.socketpair on Windows, not by deliberate local services. Deliberate local-service tests number 3. On Linux socketpair is AF_UNIX and would not be counted at all, so this figure is platform-specific and is a must-not-block population, not a debt.
notes.sweep_not_truncated: The sweep was not bounded: the full suite ran in every mode. The only reduction is dedup of repeat attempts by (nodeid, host, transport), declared in netguard.py.
notes.residual_after_fixes: CI on the merged head reports 26 tests attempting network: the 22 baselined plus the guard's own 4 deliberate probes. 0 stale baseline entries, so the frozen list is exactly the current population.

notes.local_strict_run_CORRECTION: An earlier version of this artifact said the full local strict run was killed and produced no result. THAT WAS WRONG. It ran to completion: '2 failed, 5026 passed, 2 skipped, 21 deselected in 1355.36s', and reported 26 tests attempting network, matching CI's 26 exactly. Whether it terminated a sibling lane's run instead is unresolved.
notes.local_strict_two_failures_explained: Both failures were SELF-INFLICTED by running `git merge --ff-only` ~10 minutes into a 22-minute suite, mutating the working tree under a running instrument. Proof rather than assertion: at the pre-merge commit 7e84e736, app/spine/outcomes.py defined r_multiple_from_pnl at line 79; at the merged head that function is RETIRED (line 224 is a retirement comment left by a sibling T-26 lane). The run therefore held the OLD test module in memory while reading NEW source from disk. test_deploy_gate's staleness case is the same shape: it compared an in-memory control declaration (evidence 2026-08-19) against a git last-touch recomputed from the mutated tree (2026-08-20). Both PASS on the stable merged tree: 22 passed, 0 network attempts. This is a 'state your snapshot' violation committed by me: the snapshot changed mid-flight, so the output was confidently wrong.
notes.deploy_gate_control_is_silent_on_ci: Pre-existing and already declared in the codebase, not a discovery, but worth naming: tools/deploy_gate/gate.py:297 returns 'unverifiable' when `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is true, and CI clones shallow. So the evidence-staleness control can only ever fire in a full local clone, never in CI. Outside this lane's scope; not touched.
